atc.cache1Body: query MongoDB by generic_name and atc_code with case-insensitive regex.
atc.cache2Body: if no local hit, query ChEMBL API.
atc.cache3Body: external response is normalized and persisted locally before returning to frontend.
atc.cache4Body: autocomplete receives stable payload for consistent rendering.
atc.p1: The pharmacological module uses WHO ATC classification and external ChEMBL queries only as fallback, following a local redundancy pattern aligned with the Orpha dictionary.
atc.level2Example: A16 - Other alimentary tract and metabolism products
atc.level3Example: A16A - Other products for alimentary tract and metabolism disorders
atc.title: 3. ATC Pharmacological System (WHO) and ChEMBL

sprec.p1: The SPREC code consolidates critical pre-analytical sample metadata. BioAvanceD-v2 records seven axes for fluids and seven axes for solids, ensuring laboratory reproducibility and pre-analytical chain auditing.
sprec.title: 4. Sample Quality (SPREC)

index.merkle: 5. Chain of Custody and Merkle Tree
index.title: Index

merkle.p1: Sample integrity is ensured by SHA-256 cryptographic hashing and evidence chaining for posterior verification. Each relevant change triggers signature recomputation according to governance policies.
merkle.p2: This model preserves consistency across clinical registration, pre-analytical quality and pharmacology, enabling end-to-end technical auditing in regulated environments.
merkle.title: 5. Chain of Custody and Merkle Tree

miabis.p1: BioAvanceD-v2 adopts MIABIS 2.0 as the interoperability basis for patient, specimen and quality metadata description. The operational model is relational and traceability-oriented, with cardinality Patient -> N Samples.
miabis.p2: To ensure clinical registration idempotency, the system applies heuristic matching: search by patientID or by Normalized Name + Birth Date. Normalization removes accents and standardizes casing and spacing. When matched, new data is linked to the existing patient to prevent duplicates.

table.metaRule: Validation of type, origin, protocol, quality and institution
table.patientRule: Idempotent identification by patientID or Normalized Name + Birth Date
table.sampleRule: Mandatory linkage to a valid patient before consolidating the record

miabis.title: 1. MIABIS 2.0 (Minimum Information About Biobank Data Sharing)

orpha.bullet2: Complementary relations: ICD-10 and OMIM for clinical interoperability.
orpha.bullet3: Quality blocking rule: missing mandatory biomarkers downgrades validation status.
orpha.p1: The clinical domain uses Orphanet ontologies to map rare diagnosis, related codes and semantic context for analysis. The clinical validation layer applies a rules graph to condition sample operational state based on required minimum clinical completion.
orpha.p2: In practice, samples with rare diagnosis and missing mandatory biomarkers remain completion-restricted until clinical data is provided, preserving quality and regulatory traceability.
orpha.title: 2. Orphadata and Clinical Validation
